title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated video and synthetic testimonials to create a false identity for a real, named attorney. The failure is not a malfunction of a deployed AI product but a deliberate misuse of generative AI tools by outside actors. The technology was used to fabricate deepfake videos and hundreds of fake social media profiles, giving the fraud the surface appearance of a legitimate legal practice.

The deployment point where harm occurred was social media, where the fake profiles directed victims to WhatsApp for follow-up and then to digital payment platforms to collect money. The scale, nearly 6,500 profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, indicates the content ran without effective platform-level detection for an extended period. Catching it required the attorney's own firm to hire a specialist anti-piracy company, meaning no automated or human platform review stopped the profiles before victims were reached.

What is not established is who created the deepfakes, where they operated from, or whether any platform's policies were formally found to have been violated. The reporting documents the harm and the removal effort but does not record any law enforcement finding or attribution of the fraud to a specific person or group.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate artificial intelligence scam. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating him to defraud vulnerable immigrants. In these deepfakes, a digital version of Leal promotes fraudulent immigration services, including offering US residency assistance for $2,200 to undocumented immigrants without deportation orders. The scams typically direct victims through social media videos to contact phone numbers via WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payments through digital payment apps like Venmo and Zelle.

Leal discovered the scheme last October when potential clients began calling his office, but the situation has dramatically worsened in recent months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms: 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scam also features AI-generated testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal's services. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the fraud's origin.
